rationale: A wins because it makes the missing evidence the story, not a footnote: "Deel's compliance tool is a bet that AI can read 150 countries' labor law — with no accuracy numbers" is the cleanest reporter-shaped angle in either set. B has usable bones, but it reaches for a grander trend with "the category is moving from drafting tasks into liability-bearing decisions," and one product launch cannot carry that without outside proof. A also does the harder PR work: it tells the founder where the pitch blows up before the journalist does.
gaps_in_A: "Deel is giving away the compliance layer it used to sell" overstates the facts. The update says the new AI tool is included for existing customers; it does not say Deel previously sold that layer separately or that there is no renewal-price catch.

"compresses the ground under standalone compliance vendors" is a plausible business angle, but the update gives no competitor count, pricing data, or named standalone vendors. A correctly asks for proof, but the headline gets a half-step ahead of the evidence.

"Misclassification carries real statutory penalties" is probably true, but it is external context, not in the supplied update. Fine as a reporting premise, not fine as an unsupported claim in a blind-grounded angle set.

"newsjack-detector" as the next step is a little mis-aimed. The launch is already a current peg; the more urgent move is getting accuracy data, liability posture, and one customer or employment-law source.
gaps_in_B: "deciding whether your contractor is legally an employee" makes the tool sound like it renders a final legal decision. The update says it flags risks; that difference matters in compliance copy unless you enjoy subpoenas as a hobby.
"the category is moving from drafting tasks into liability-bearing decisions" is trend inflation. One Deel launch is evidence for a question, not proof of a category shift.

"tracks all 150 in real time" is invented. The update says the tool checks across 150 countries as a company hires; it does not say real-time legal updating or jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction maintenance.
"free" and "lock-in" are smart but under-proven. "Included for existing customers" is not the same as free forever, no renewal increase, or an explicit lock-in strategy.
